resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com places the tower 13 miles northeast of Rathdrum. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1950 item that says 16 miles northeast of Coeur d'Alene, and a 1940 survey description that says 15 miles NNE of Coeur d'Alene. The distances differ, but all describe the same Kootenai County peak; the story does not repeat the distances.

The Forest Lookouts page and Idaho Fire Lookouts both list a crow's nest (c.1929) and a 20-foot pole tower (c.1934) but do not say whether the tower replaced the crow's nest. Both are recorded as built, and the story does not claim a replacement.

notes_for_editor: Kootenai County, Coeur d'Alene NF, the crow's nest c.1929, the 20-foot L-4 tower c.1934 and the 1959 destruction agree across three pages. The Forest Lookouts page attributes its dates to Kresek, and the other two appear to draw on the same older record, so this is one underlying source rather than three independent ones. Brief coordinates 47.88222, -116.6381 match the firelookout.org list (Cedar Mountain, Kootenai, Tower Gone), which we read as the index page at https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/id; that page is not cited in the story. Do not confuse this site with us-id-cedar-mountain-2, the St. Joe National Forest peak in Shoshone County (47.33006, -115.83358). The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1940 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description for the tower, which may help place the site but was not checked on the ground. The sources give no date for any 'Removed' event, and none describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to the public, so the access object is omitted from facts. The brief's events list had only 1959 destroyed; the 1929 and 1934 builds and the 1950 radio item are added.
